answer: Agents must continuously solve a memory-hard basalt cipher parameterized by a sliding canyon of real-time beacon outputs; each solution requires exclusive, low-latency access to a physically unique hardware-bound DRAM controller, strictly proving single-tenancy. The canyon width scales with network size, forcing sybil operators to provision dedicated memory bandwidth per-identity at marginal cost of dollars per epoch, making large-scale fabrication economically prohibitive.
